claims.text: The anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr arises from local internal stresses generated by thermal-expansion mismatch between chemically heterogeneous regions.
Chemical short-range order amplifies local thermal-expansion mismatch.
Mismatch-induced internal stresses slow dislocation migration.
Chemical short-range order alters plastic-zone development in HfNbTaTiZr.
Heat treatment can establish enhanced chemical short-range order in the proposed HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
Rapid quenching can preserve a minimally ordered, random atomic configuration in the proposed HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
Chemical short-range order introduces lattice distortions.
Thermal exposure causes chemically distinct regions of HfNbTaTiZr to expand by different amounts.
Short-range-ordered regions expand differently from more disordered regions.
The resulting localized internal stress fields act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Slow dislocation migration produces limited relaxation of the indentation dislocation network and negligible dislocation emission into the sample interior.
Compared with the random alloy, short-range-ordered HfNbTaTiZr will have higher elastic moduli at high temperatures.
Compared with the random alloy, short-range-ordered HfNbTaTiZr will have greater tensile-creep resistance at 1250 °C.
Compared with the random alloy, short-range-ordered HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit higher dislocation density during nanoindentation.
Compared with the random alloy, short-range-ordered HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit larger plastic zones during nanoindentation.
Thermal cycling will make the mechanical differences between ordered and random specimens especially prominent.
A homogeneous random atomic distribution minimizes local thermal-expansion mismatch caused by chemical heterogeneity.
The proposed mechanism governs behavior from approximately 293 K to 1250 °C.
The mismatch-based mechanism explains the alloy's reported high creep resistance, cold-rolling microhardness increase, and temperature-dependent elastic moduli.
